title: Mood and Substance State Modifiers in ADHD and Bipolar-Spectrum Differential Diagnosis
background: This module evaluates episodic mood effects and the cognitive, psychotic, activation, and mood-stability effects of cannabis/THC, prescription stimulants, and nicotine in ADHD and bipolar-spectrum contexts.
population: Adolescents and adults with ADHD, bipolar-spectrum disorder, both conditions, substance exposure, or relevant control groups.
intervention: Hypomanic, manic, mixed, or psychotic state; cannabis or THC; prescribed stimulant; nicotine; medication change; or interactions among these exposures.
comparator: Euthymia, abstinence, placebo, adequate sleep, unexposed controls, or within-person baseline.

outcomes_primary.name: Attention, executive function, speech, irritability, salience, impulsivity, psychosis, and mood instability
Evidence distinguishing lifelong traits from episodic state effects

outcomes_secondary.name: Dose, timing, interaction, confounding, and vulnerability factors

inclusion: Adolescent or adult sample relevant to ADHD, bipolar-spectrum illness, cannabis/THC, prescription stimulants, or nicotine.
Reports cognitive, activation, manic, psychotic, speech, salience, impulse-control, or functional outcomes.
Provides empirical results or an authoritative professional guideline/evidence synthesis.
exclusion: Non-prescription stimulant exposure with no relevance to prescribed ADHD treatment or bipolar differential diagnosis.
No separable exposure or outcome relevant to claim H8.
Opinion, commercial treatment page, protocol, or unsourced narrative.
Case report retained only as a safety signal, not as causal or incidence evidence.

analysis.effect_measure: Narrative safety and differential-diagnosis synthesis; no cross-exposure pooling.

registration: Protocol frozen for AI-assisted rapid review on 2026-07-29; not prospectively registered.
disclaimer: AI Reviewer-1 rapid-review draft. Human Reviewer 2 and clinical sign-off remain pending. Not diagnostic or treatment guidance.
